sentences.text: Onchopristis is an extinct genus of sawskate found in Cretaceous deposits across North Africa, Europe, North America, and possibly South America.
This animal possessed a long rostrum with large denticles, a feature similar to the 'saws' of modern sawfishes and sawsharks.
The rostral saw of Onchopristis was made of cartilage and was compressed from top to bottom.
The denticles on the sides of Onchopristis's rostrum were larger than those at the front, with the largest measuring 7 centimeters.
The skull base (neurocranium) of Onchopristis was rectangular and box-like in shape.
Onchopristis had a large orbital cavity, or eye socket.
The oral teeth of Onchopristis had well-developed cutting edges that extended continuously from the main cusp to the side cusplets.
Onchopristis had a long, paddle-shaped snout lined on both sides with hook-shaped barbed teeth.
The evolution of the saw-like rostrum in Onchopristis is an example of 'pristification,' a trait that evolved independently multiple times among cartilaginous fish.
Onchopristis appeared in the first episode of the British documentary Planet Dinosaur.
The genus Onchopristis was originally described by Ernst Stromer in 1917.
In 1905, Émile Haug named the species Gigantichthys numidus based on fragmentary rostral denticles found in Algeria.
Ernst Stromer assigned the species to the new genus Onchopristis in 1917.
The species Onchopristis dunklei was named by Charles McNulty, Jr. and Bob Slaughter in 1962.
The snout likely possessed electroreceptors to detect prey underwater, similar to modern sharks.
Onchopristis may have raked river beds to find and devour its prey.
Fossil evidence shows that Spinosaurus preyed on Onchopristis, indicated by rostral denticles found within Spinosaurus jaws in North Africa.
Teeth of Spinosaurus and rostral denticles of Onchopristis are found together in a bone bed in the Kem Kem beds of Morocco.
The genus Onchopristis is classified under the authority of Villalobos-Segura, Kriwet, Vullo, Stumpf, Ward, and Underwood in 2021.
Onchopristis is classified within the family Pristidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Onchopristis as a member of the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Onchopristis lived in coastal and river deposits from the Barremian to Cenomanian ages (approximately 125 to 94 million years ago), making it one of the oldest known sclerorhynchoids.
Onchopristis lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Fossils of Onchopristis date from the Barremian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 125.77 and 66 million years ago.
Remains of Onchopristis have been found in North America, South America, North Africa, and New Zealand.
Some researchers suggest that the two valid species of Onchopristis might actually be a single taxon with morphological variation due to its wide geographical range.
It is debated whether rostral denticles found in Mali belong to Onchopristis numida or are actually cutlassfish fangs.

There is a debate regarding the assignment of a 1.46-meter rostrum and denticles from Egypt's Dakhla Formation to Onchopristis, with some researchers arguing they belong to a different sclerorhynchoid.
In the documentary Planet Dinosaur, Onchopristis is depicted as anadromous, spawning in rivers and being preyed upon by the dinosaur Spinosaurus.
